CGA never looked that good 30 years ago.

That's very true. The list of CGA games that actually used the card's 16-colour modes/tweaks is pretty short (Ctrl+F "All Known Games") – as was the list of programmers who even knew about them. CGA was widely believed to be 4 colour graphics only.

Interestingly, it was only this year —some 33 or 34 years after CGA was first released— that some 1337 demosceners figured out how to get up to 1024 colours out of a CGA card. As some commentator observed, had those bytes been on a disk in 1981, they could have had this back then, but they didn't. Nobody knew. It took over three decades for people to come along and teach that very old dog these new tricks. In light of the 1024 colour demo, 16 colours seem like an old hat, but unlike the 16 colour modes where at least some games exist (see above), as best I know, nobody has written a CGA 1024 colour game yet. (Actually, it might be better to use just 512 colours, because the 1024 mode eats up too many clockcycles – not sure if there'd be any left for even checking the keyboard. If yes, then you might be able to write some kind of adventure game with static, slideshow 1024 colour images. Otherwise, if you want actual onscreen movement etc., you'll probably have to limit yourself to 512 colours.)

Right now you have a system of submitters and mods. I think it would be nice to introduce a new layer: Subscribe to feeds that overlay the content.

Take for example how adblock feeds work for Chrome or Firefox. Imagine there are 30 independent editors who publish a feed that modifies what you see here on the forums. They could publish:

  • Marking a story as duplicate
  • A replacement headline for a particular URL / link. One that they edit that reflects their explanation of why a story is interesting. Not just consuming the original source headline.
  • A twitter-length summary to go along with the headline.
  • A star-rating 0 to 10 that advises if they recommend this particular link.
  • Category tags / NSFL tags, trigger tags, controversy tags, location tags, etc

Then multiple editors could compete to publish the best "rewrites" of headlines. And people could filter and choose which editor / reviewer they overlay the content with.

Take something like the Google Play Store for Android Apps: Imagine being able to pick the App reviewers you follow and to be able to filter based on that criteria when you search the app store. This idea has value beyond just reddit-style forums.

The feeds could be published in a technical format right on the website itself in a specific /v/ for publishing feeds. Each feed publisher would start a thread... The author of the feed could edit the message as the day continues to reflect changes and new additions. The existing /u/username system could be used to identify which feeds to subscribe to, etc. This would eliminate the need to depend on outside websites for feeds...

I created a mockup of an example of how a feed could be published: https://voat.co/v/headlinefeeds/comments/113089

Feedback welcome.
